summary: This note is a collection of passages about Hyderabad, India, covering its transport, media, public health indicators, history, etymology, economy, traffic, and civic administration. It describes the city's founding in 1591, its time as capital of the Nizams, its growth from a pearl-trading and manufacturing city into an IT and financial services centre, and the bodies (GHMC, HMDA) that govern it.
one_line: Overview of Hyderabad, India: its history and name origins, economy, transport, media, health statistics, and municipal governance.
key_facts: Hyderabad was established in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah and remained under the Qutb Shahi dynasty for nearly a century before the Mughals captured the region.
In 1724 Mughal viceroy Asif Jah I declared his sovereignty and founded the Nizams of Hyderabad dynasty; in 1769 the city became the formal capital of the Nizams.
In 1798 the Nizam signed a subsidiary alliance with the East India Company, allowing the British Indian Army to occupy Bolarum (modern Secunderabad).
Hyderabad State joined the Indian Union in 1948, and the city became capital of Andhra Pradesh after the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
In 2014 Telangana split from Andhra Pradesh and Hyderabad became joint capital of both states, an arrangement scheduled to end by 2025.

The name Hyderabad means "Haydar's city" or "lion city", honouring Caliph Ali Ibn Abi Talib, also known as Haydar; a popular theory says the city was first named Bhagyanagar after Bhagmati, who took the title Hyder Mahal.
Hyderabad is nicknamed "City of Pearls" and until the 18th century was the only global trading centre for large diamonds.
As of 2012 there were over 3.5 million vehicles in the city (74% two-wheelers, 15% cars, 3% three-wheelers), while roads cover only 9.5% of the city area.

The Multi-Modal Transport System (MMTS) is a three-line suburban rail service used by over 160,000 passengers daily; Secunderabad Railway Station is the largest station and South Central Railway zone headquarters.

The Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC), formed in April 2007, covers 650 km2 with 18 circles and 150 wards; after the 2016 election the Telangana Rashtra Samithi formed the majority and the Mayor is Bonthu Ram Mohan.
In the 2005 National Family Health Survey, Hyderabad's total fertility rate was 1.8, infant mortality was 35 per 1,000 live births, and only 61% of children had all basic vaccines.
Television broadcasting began in 1974 with Doordarshan; private satellite channels began in July 1992 with Star TV; the first public internet access began in 1995.
The HMDA is an apolitical urban planning agency covering the GHMC and suburbs across 54 mandals in five districts.
